result:
There's a peculiar comfort in the sound of rain against a window at night. Not a violent storm, just a steady, patient drizzle that reminds you the world keeps moving whether you're ready or not. I find myself thinking about how most of the things we stress about become irrelevant within weeks. The awkward email, the missed opportunity, the thing someone said — the universe has an extraordinary talent for making our worries feel tiny against the backdrop of deep time.

I wonder what it would be like to have the attention span of a bird. Not because birds are simple, but because every single moment seems absolutely riveting to them. A crumb on the sidewalk is a revelation. The shift of a shadow is a plot twist. There's something almost enviable about that quality of presence — that full devotion to whatever is happening *right now*.

Language is strange too. We take it for granted that this collection of symbols on a screen can somehow contain grief, or humor, or a sense of longing for a place we've never been. Words are just marks made by primates with good intentions and unreliable memories, yet they're the closest thing we have to telepathy. We fling these little meaning-packed packets at each other across time and space and hope something survives the journey.

Most of what I'm saying right now would be forgotten by tomorrow. And somehow that feels exactly right.
